title: Implement immutable billing event stream with queryable provenance for audits
creator: Ravi Kapoor
description:
Background:
Redwood must provide tamper-evident, queryable records of billing and quota enforcement decisions to satisfy SOC/ISO audits and customer inquiries. Current logs are scattered across request proxy, runtime, and billing pipelines which makes reproducible audit trails difficult and increases reconciliation churn.

Goal:
Create an append-only billing event stream that captures canonical usage and enforcement decisions with cryptographic provenance and a queryable interface for auditors and internal reconciliation. The stream must support high-throughput writes, be cost-effective for long-term retention, and integrate with existing billing pipelines during rollout.

Key design elements (proposed):
- Canonical event schema: every billing-related event will include event_id, request_id, customer_id, account_id, model_version, tokens_consumed, token_cost_estimate, generation_direction (prompt/response), latency_ms, rate_limit_outcome (allowed/blocked/throttled), quota_snapshot (remaining/limit/window), routing_variant, serving_node_id, batch_id (if batched), server_timestamp_iso8601, ingest_timestamp_iso8601, and signature (batch level).
- Append-only stream: use a partitioned, append-only store (initial implementation on Kafka/Managed PubSub or Kinesis depending on region) with an immutable write-ahead manifest saved to WORM cloud storage (GCS/S3 Object Lock) for monthly anchoring.
- Batch signing and anchoring: sign batches with a service key protected by KMS/HSM and write signed manifests to zero-trust object storage to provide tamper evidence. Cryptographic checksums per file and an anchored ledger entry will be produced for auditors.
- Dual-write rollout: initially dual-write canonical events alongside current logging (edge/proxy logs + runtime traces) for a minimum 6-week reconciliation window. A reconciliation job will detect drift and missing events with automated alerts.
- Query interface & exports: provide an auditor-facing read-only query API that can reconstruct usage for any contiguous time window, including raw event export (parquet/ndjson) and pre-built invoice reconciliation bundles. Exports must include the signing metadata to verify provenance.
- Retention & tiers: hot storage (searchable) for 90 days, warm for 1 year, archived cold storage with WORM for 7 years for compliance customers. Retention tiers controlled by account plan and exportability settings.
- Access controls & RBAC: introduce RBAC roles specific to audit access (roles: billing-audit, sec-audit, legal-read) with scoped access to the event stream and signed manifests. Access must be logged and included in SOC evidence.
- Monitoring & SLOs: metrics for write latency, batch signing latency, event loss rate, reconciliation drift, and query latency. SLO: 99.9% of events committed within 30s of request completion.

Acceptance criteria (must be demonstrable):
1) Defined canonical schema, with JSON Schema and protobuf definitions stored in the repo.
2) Working prototype dual-writing canonical events from proxy and runtime into managed stream in us-east-1 with signed batch manifests written to WORM S3.
3) Nightly reconciliation job that reports >99.95% event parity between old logs and new canonical stream over a 2-week period.
4) Auditor query endpoint that returns a verifiable export (signed manifest + data bundle) for a requested time window, including checksums.
5) RBAC roles created with audit logging enabled; example SOC evidence bundle (export + access log + manifest verification) is produced.
6) Documentation and runbook for incident handling when reconciliation drift >0.1% for a day.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: finalize schema, sign-off with Billing PM and Security (create JSON Schema + proto), KMS key request, and design review.
- Week 2: implement producer library for canonical events in runtime service and proxy; stub managed stream in dev.
- Week 3: implement batch signer service and manifest writer to WORM S3; unit + integration tests for signature verification.
- Week 4: enable dual-write in staging; build reconciliation job and dashboards; security review and penetration checklist.
- Weeks 5-8: canary dual-write in production on a subset of accounts, run reconciliation, fix drift classes, update docs, present SOC evidence artifacts to compliance.

Rollout & fallbacks:
- Feature-flagged producer: can disable canonical writes if signers fail.
- If signer/KMS unavailable, stream will buffer but route to a quarantine bucket and emit high-severity alert to on-call.
- Read API will fallback to pre-signed, historical exports for up-to-90-day queries until queryable hot store is populated.

Open questions / risks:
- Cost: long-term storage and per-query costs for deep-history exports. Need pricing model for customers requiring 7-year WORM retention.
- Regional compliance: certain customers require in-region WORM storage and HSM; estimating engineering effort to support per-region anchoring.
- Latency: signing each batch adds latency; must quantify impact on commit windows and reconciler SLOs.
- Data minimization: ensure event schema balances auditability with PII minimization (avoid storing full prompt text unless required and consented).

- Ravi Kapoor: submit KMS/HSM key request and permissions for signer service (due 2025-02-20).
- SRE (tbd): provision managed stream topic and S3 bucket with Object Lock in staging (due 2025-02-24).

Notes on SOC evidence artifacts to produce for compliance review:
- Signed manifest chain for sample invoice window (one month), plus exported data bundle and verification script.
- Access logs showing who retrieved the bundle and when, tied to RBAC role.
- Reconciliation report showing parity with legacy billing logs and any corrective actions taken.

This ticket coordinates cross-functional work between Runtime, Billing Pipeline, SRE, Security, and Compliance. Expect multiple follow-up tickets for regionalization, storage-cost optimization, and audit UI in Console.
